pool.q: How is raster data stored?
options: As a grid of values rendered on a map as pixels
As a list of map labels
pool.explain: Rasters suit continuous surfaces such as elevation or temperature.
pool.evidence: Raster data is stored as a grid of values which are rendered on a map as pixels.

pool.q: What do vector data structures represent?
options: Specific features on the Earth's surface along with their attributes
pool.explain: Vectors come as points, lines and polygons.
pool.evidence: Vector data structures represent specific features on the Earth's surface along with attributes of those features.

pool.q: In vector data, what are vertices?
options: Discrete geometric locations (x, y values) that define the shape of a spatial object
pool.explain: Points have one vertex; lines and polygons have many.
pool.evidence: Vectors are composed of discrete geometric locations (x, y values) known as vertices that define the shape of the spatial object.

pool.q: Which geospatial datasets are associated with a coordinate reference system (CRS)?
options: All geospatial datasets, raster and vector
pool.explain: Layers must share (or be reprojected to) the same CRS to line up.
pool.evidence: All geospatial datasets (raster and vector) are associated with a specific coordinate reference system.

pool.q: What is the relationship between a CRS and an SRS?
options: An SRS is a type of raster
They are synonyms and are commonly interchanged
A CRS is only used for oceans
An SRS replaces latitude and longitude
pool.explain: Both describe how coordinates map to places on Earth.
pool.evidence: CRS (coordinate reference system) and SRS (spatial reference system) are synonyms and are commonly interchanged.

pool.q: What is QGIS?
options: A professional, free and open-source GIS application
pool.explain: GRASS GIS is another open-source platform.
pool.evidence: QGIS is a professional GIS application that is built on top of and proud to be itself Free and Open Source Software (FOSS).

pool.q: Which organisation supports open-source GIS platforms such as QGIS?
pool.explain: OSGeo supports several actively managed GIS platforms.
pool.evidence: The Open Source Geospatial Foundation (OSGEO) supports several actively managed GIS platforms

pool.q: What is an orbit?
options: The curved path a satellite follows around the Earth due to gravity
pool.explain: The orbit affects a dataset's resolution and revisit time.
pool.evidence: An orbit is the curved path a satellite follows around the Earth due to gravitational force.

pool.q: What is spectroscopy?
options: Measuring how materials interact with electromagnetic radiation across the spectrum
pool.explain: Scientists measure it from the ground and from ships too.
pool.evidence: Spectroscopy is the measurement of how materials interact with electromagnetic radiation across the spectrum.

pool.q: What does a dataset's 'version' distinguish?
options: Versions of a data product made with different processing or calibration
pool.explain: Using the latest version is encouraged.
pool.evidence: Version is used to distinguish between versions of a given data product

pool.q: What does the Spatial Extent element of a dataset describe?
options: The geographic coverage of the data
pool.explain: Temporal extent describes when the data was acquired.
pool.evidence: The Spatial Extent element describes the geographic coverage of the data.

pool.q: What is spatial (horizontal) resolution?
options: How often a satellite revisits an area
The smallest horizontal distance between successive data elements
pool.explain: Finer resolution shows smaller features.
pool.evidence: is defined as the smallest horizontal distance between successive elements of data in a dataset

pool.q: What does the cloud icon on an Earthdata dataset page mean?
options: The dataset is stored in the cloud rather than on-premises
The data is about weather only
pool.explain: Nearly all of NASA's Earth science data is accessible through Earthdata Cloud.
pool.evidence: The cloud icon indicates the dataset lives in the cloud as opposed to on-premises.

pool.q: NASA EOSDIS data products are processed at levels ranging from…
pool.explain: Higher levels are more processed — from raw instrument data to model outputs.
pool.evidence: data products are processed at various levels ranging from Level 0 to Level 4.

pool.q: A shapefile is made of several files. What must you do when moving it on your computer?
options: Always move and keep all the files together
pool.explain: The geometry, attributes, index and projection live in separate files.
pool.evidence: It is important when moving files on your computer to always move and keep all four files together.

pool.q: Why does the lesson use QGIS rather than ArcGIS?
options: ArcGIS is very expensive and Windows-only; QGIS runs on Windows, Mac and Linux
QGIS is made by the government
pool.explain: QGIS has most functions historians commonly need.
pool.evidence: ArcGIS is prohibitively expensive and only runs on Windows

pool.q: What is a CRS in QGIS?
options: The map projection: a way to represent real places on a flat map
pool.explain: Layers need a matching CRS to line up correctly.
pool.evidence: The CRS is the map projection and projections are the various ways to represent real world places on two-dimensional maps.

pool.q: Why is Prince Edward Island a good example for the QGIS lessons?
options: Lots of free data is online and it is small, so downloads are quick
pool.explain: Choosing a small, well-documented area makes practice easier.
pool.evidence: PEI is a great example because there is a lot of data for free online and because it is Canada's smallest province

pool.q: How are layers ordered in the QGIS layers panel?
options: In descending order of visibility — the top layer appears on top in the viewer
By the date they were created
pool.explain: Drag layers to change which ones cover others.
pool.evidence: These layers are organized in descending order of visibility

pool.q: What are the two basic types of data structures for geographic data?
pool.explain: Vectors store points, lines and polygons; rasters store grids of cells.
pool.evidence: Vector layers are, along with raster layers, one of the two basic types of data structures that store data.

pool.q: What can point features represent?
options: Specific locations, such as towns, buildings or events
pool.explain: Lines represent roads and rivers; polygons represent areas.
pool.evidence: Points can be used to represent specific locations, such as towns, buildings, events, etc.

pool.q: Who needs georeferencing?
options: Anyone who wants to accurately digitise data found on a paper map
pool.explain: Georeferencing stretches a scanned map so it fits real geographic coordinates.
pool.evidence: Georeferencing is required for anyone who wants to accurately digitize data found on a paper map

pool.q: What knowledge does georeferencing a historical map require?
options: Both the geography and the history of the place
pool.explain: You need to know which features still exist in the same place.
pool.evidence: Georeferencing a historical map requires a knowledge of both the geography and the history of the place you are studying to ensure accuracy.

pool.q: Why check that your control points have stayed in the same place over time?
options: Control points are chosen at random
Built and natural landscapes change over time
pool.explain: Houses, intersections or towns used as control points must still match.
pool.evidence: The built and natural landscapes change over time, and it is important to confirm that the location of your control points

pool.q: To make a basic choropleth map of counties with Folium, what do you join your data to?
options: Shape files that define county boundaries
pool.explain: Each county polygon is then coloured by its data value.
pool.evidence: This will include joining your data to 'shape files' that define county boundaries, which will allow you to create a basic choropleth map.

pool.q: What are choropleth maps good for?
options: Discovering and showing patterns that are otherwise hard to see
pool.explain: Areas are shaded by the value of a variable.
pool.evidence: Choropleth maps are an excellent tool for discovering and demonstrating patterns in data that might be otherwise hard to discern.

pool.q: Why use Folium to build interactive maps?
options: You only need Python, not JavaScript or CSS
pool.explain: Folium builds web maps from Python code.
pool.evidence: This will allow you to create a wide variety of interactive maps without needing to know JavaScript or CSS

pool.q: What does the 'shades of purple' example say about election maps?
options: Every region votes the same way
Election maps should use one colour
Most regions are mixed rather than all one colour
pool.explain: Two-colour maps can hide how mixed most places are.
pool.evidence: But most regions are not all red or all blue: most are shades of purple

pool.q: On a choropleth map, how should you colour areas with missing data?
options: With a colour distinct from the palette, so it is clear data is missing
With the same colour as zero
Leave them out of the map entirely
pool.explain: Otherwise readers may mistake missing data for low values.
pool.evidence: This color should be distinct from the palette colors, so it is clear that data is missing.

pool.q: Why does a choropleth map become uninformative when most values fall into one or two bins?
options: Most areas end up the same colour
pool.explain: Transforming the data or adjusting bins can reveal more.
pool.evidence: when the vast majority of cases are contained in just one or two bins, the map becomes somewhat uninformative

pool.q: In the police shootings map, what did grey counties mean?
options: No cases were recorded for them in the data
pool.explain: Missing data should be coloured distinctly from the palette.
pool.evidence: The grey counties are those for which the Post have not recorded any cases of fatal police shootings.

pool.q: What is the second element passed to Folium's choropleth function?
options: The variable used to colour the map
pool.explain: The first element identifies the geographic regions.
pool.evidence: The second element is the variable to be used to draw the choropleth map's colors.

pool.q: What does Folium generate when it creates a choropleth map?
options: Underlying GeoJSON data about each region
pool.explain: Information boxes read their values from this data.
pool.evidence: When Folium creates a choropleth map, it generates underlying GeoJSON data about each geographic region.

pool.q: What is JSON?
options: A standard format for sending information around the internet
pool.explain: Its data is organised as key : value pairs.
pool.evidence: The JSON data format is a standard way of sending information around the internet.
